pr_title: Fix `scroll_offset_changed` signal emitting every time graph is re-drawn
pr_body:
This fix ensures `GraphEdit`'s `scroll_offset_changed` signal is fired only when the scroll values are actually changed.
Contains a small related fix to prevent regression of the issue with `AnimationNodeBlendTreeEditor` resetting scroll view when a connection is made.

*Bugsquad edit:* Fixes #76270

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.

pr_comments: Note that we have `set_value_no_signal()` method now, which sets the value without emitting the signal. I think `setting_scroll_ofs` could be removed entirely now (perhaps).

> Note that we have `set_value_no_signal()` method now, which sets the value without emitting the signal. I think `setting_scroll_ofs` could be removed entirely now (perhaps).

Oh that's good to know, I'll have another look at it and make a new commit to make this PR a bit cleaner.

Unfortunately after taking another look `set_value_no_signal` doesn't solve any of the problems here, as the `_scroll_moved` event when the scroll values are changed is no longer called at all, and it needs to be called to update the graph view.

I think the current version of this PR is as good as I can come up of how to fix the issues, with the knowledge that GraphEdit's going to get reworked at some point anyway.
Would like to request a review of this PR again please.

issue_context.title: `GraphEdit` emits `scroll_offset_changed` signal in cases where scroll_offset hasn't changed
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.2.stable

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

When using GraphEdit, the scroll_offset_changed signal will emit under circumstances where you wouldn't expect/it shouldn't be emitting, where the scroll_offset has not actually changed.

Noticeably this happens when adding a new GraphNode child, as well as if you just click on the graph without moving it at all.

### Steps to reproduce

Using the reproduction project attached, go into the Offset Demo plugin screen at the top next to AssetLib.
Open the output window to see messages for when the scroll_offset is changed.

Add a node to the graph using the 'Add node' button and see the scroll offset signal occurring, without the offset ever changing.
Clicking on the graph will also cause the behaviour.

(The repro project was edited in the 4.1 development branch to check it still existed but this behaviour was first observed on 4.0.2.stable.)

### Minimal reproduction project

[scroll offset minrepro.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/11277908/scroll.offset.minrepro.zip)
comments:
Found that this bug occurs because the scroll_offset_changed signal is emitted in _update_scroll_offset, which is called every time the graph is redrawn for any reason whatsoever.

This seems to be an issue introduced by the fix for #72479.

Made a PR at #76322, need some guidance on whether how I've implemented the fix is within the project's guidelines, and whether what I've deleted has effects on other types of graphs in the editor I'm not aware of that people more familiar will be able to point out.

review_comments: I'm pretty sure this is required to center the view on the blend tree.

This double use of the same flag is too convoluted and unreliable. I think the overall solution can be as simple as storing the the last offset and checking if it has changed before emitting the signal.
Moving it here means that we will emit the signal before the value has been updated, which is incorrect.
If the added method is supposed to be private, it needs to be put into the appropriate section above.
